title: Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups

issues.description: This is a coverage limit, not a defect. These sections build the terminal malnormal quasiconvex VCS peripheral family and the exact intersection transfer. Theorem boundary:good-fillings and Theorem boundary:primitive-vcs depend entirely on them, and they run to about 5,000 lines. I did not audit them line by line, so the primitive case cannot be certified from this review.
issues.evidence: boundary:primitive-vcs proof: 'The preceding actual-row, closure, and terminal arguments construct the finite malnormal quasiconvex virtually compact special peripheral family.'

issues.description: This is a terse step, not a failure. The selective small-cancellation step only sketches two things: that Coulon's constants are uniform over every H-invariant selection, and that the sheets in collars avoid the branch images. Both are plausible and follow the standard Dahmani-Guirardel-Osin pattern (rescale, then fill deep enough), but the overlap bound for hulls after rescaling is asserted rather than computed.
issues.evidence: 'Rescale the original space first to meet those bounds, fix the cone radius, and then make the filling deep enough to meet the translation-length bound.'

coverage: Read in full: Sec 0 (Introduction, reduction to primitive extension groups via Linton plus the companion hyperbolicity paper, Prop compact-toolkit) and Sec 1 (filling criterion). Within Sec 1 that covers the cofinite filling via MSQT, the Cohen-Lyndon free product, selective hyperbolicity via Coulon, the bounded wall collapse, sheets and the branched cubical model, the CAT(0)/flag argument, the hierarchy cut and Kurosh step for vertex stabilizers, controlled linearization, finite inverse-depth descent, recombination by perturbation, progressive characters, the BNS/Sikorav lemma, and the cd-2 free-kernel lemma via LHS and H^3(J;ZJ). I checked the logic of the flagness argument, the undistortion transfer through P->Hbar, and the LHS computation. Also read in full: Sec 2 (ascending tori). That covers the field hypotheses and the Fox matrix t^{-1}I - J (I verified the sign and invertibility derivation by hand), shift equivalence, the relative tree model, point stabilizers and malnormality, the quasiconvex peripherals, the train-track filling, the injective-block reduction (lift and uniqueness identities checked), filled VCS, and Cor ascending-finite-rank. Partially read: Sec 3 up to the subtree gate criterion (refinement, row geometry, level basis dim k-1, restriction injection, path inertia, cyclic-path dictionary). Read: the start of Sec 10 (panels, consumption, internal/completed trees, the cocycle-to-Bergeron-Wise separation lemma) and its final assembly theorems. Skimmed only, by statement: Sections 4-9 and 11.
main_claim: Every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special, i.e. it has a finite-index subgroup that is pi_1 of a compact special cube complex with a local isometry to a finite RAAG Salvetti complex. Hence, by Kielak-Linton, it is virtually free-by-cyclic. The paper also proves that hyperbolic ascending HNN extensions of finite-rank free groups are VCS and virtually (f.g. free)-by-Z.
